titulo: Final project: your site + server + battery + report
lead: The final project brings the pieces together: the page with tools, the MCP server with the same rule, the frozen battery, the log, the watch, and the approved catalog. One script runs the seven checks and writes your site's dated report. You leave with it and with the maintenance plan for when the spec changes.
objetivo: combine the seven checks into a dated report for your site and leave with the maintenance plan for when the spec changes.

The watcher is the only check that depends on the network. Without a network, it exits with 3 and the report marks "sem conclusão", not "ok".

secoes.titulo: Take the kit to your site
secoes.sub: In order. Each step has the script that proves it.

texto: Pull your site's logic off the screen into a module with no DOM, like oficinas.mjs.
The page and the server import this module. Proof: superficies.mjs.
Swap ferramentas.mjs and servidor/mcp.mjs for your own tools, with the log (observado) on both.
Proof: observar.mjs with no personal data.
Write contrato.json and casos.json for your tools and freeze them.
Proof: bateria.mjs in all four modes.
governanca.json with owner, date, and level; watcher base recorded; neighbor decisions.

exemplo.texto: Polyfill only for rehearsal, never in production. Put the origin trial token and its end date (Chrome 156) on your calendar.

perguntas.p: The report came out 6/7: the watch marked "sem conclusão". What does that tell you?
opcoes: That the spec changed and the site has to come down.
That the battery passed, but the MCP server went down.
That there was no network to read the sources; run it again with network.
That the catalog has a tool without approval.
perguntas.explica: Watch exit code 3 = it didn't read the sources. The report keeps that separate from "ok" and from "FALHA" so nobody mistakes a missing network for "nothing changed."

perguntas.p: What is the first step to bring the kit to your site?
opcoes: Move the rule out of the screen code into a module that the page and the server both import.
Publish the polyfill on the site so every visitor gets the API.
Write the battery before knowing which tools exist.
Record the watch baseline before having any tool.
perguntas.explica: Without the rule in one place, the doors drift apart (lesson 2). The polyfill is for rehearsal only; the battery and baseline come after there is something to test.

opcoes: Because GitHub Pages requires a date in the file name.
Because Chrome reads the file date to release the origin trial token.
Because MCP 2026-07-28 requires a date in every response.
Because it holds for the spec and versions of that day; after that, run it again.
perguntas.explica: WebMCP is a draft and it changes; the report is a snapshot of one day, with the 10/16/2026 spec and MCP 2026-07-28. The watch tells you when the snapshot has gone stale.

perguntas.p: Which course in the track teaches you to test the site with a real browser agent?
opcoes: Course 1, MCP server for your service.
Course 4, security between site and agent.
Course 0, foundations: how agents use a site.
perguntas.explica: Course 3 covers Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, and the agent task battery. The battery here calls the tools directly, with no model.
